clue.text: Tom's aggressive strategy, reportedly an escape mechanism

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or said, so the phrase spoken aloud gives the entry

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, whose attack plan is to bare its talons: get out claws

explanation.surface: It reads like a remark about Tom Cruise's ruthless tactics turning out to be a way of escaping something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a person (Tom Cruise is a regular in this puzzle's world), but it is a tomcat unsheathing its claws.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract provision letting a party withdraw is literally a mechanism for escaping an agreement.

clue.text: Mattis getting upset over new expletive

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the reversed nickname above the next letter
upset in a down clue means knocked over, so the nickname is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Jim Mattis, former US Defense Secretary, is nicknamed Mad Dog

explanation.surface: A news snippet: the US general, upset by something novel, swears.
explanation.walkthrough: Mattis's nickname 'Mad Dog' written backwards gives GODDAM, which sits above N.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a mild oath or curse word, an example of an expletive.

clue.text: Patrick Leahy's entertaining dribble

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the senator's name holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: It reads as if the US senator Patrick Leahy were amusing an audience with a drooling routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join: patTRICK LEahy.
explanation.definitionFit: A trickle is a thin, slow flow of liquid, which is what a dribble is.

clue.text: "New Renault"? Journalist: "Nothing's been changed!"

indicators.note: new suggests the brand name is made afresh, its letters put into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A motoring writer protests that the so-called new Renault model is just the old one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' seems to describe the car but signals rearranging RENAULT into UNALTER.
explanation.definitionFit: If nothing has been changed, everything remains as it was: the same, untouched.

clue.text: Leaders of Caerphilly young men's rugby union in Wales

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their opening letters, taken in turn

explanation.surface: A sports item about the top players in a Caerphilly youth rugby side in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Caerphilly is a town in south Wales, where rugby union is the national sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Cymru is the Welsh-language name of the country, so it is a translation of the definition.

clue.text: Postmortem of K-pop star crushed by car

indicators.note: in a down clue, the singer being crushed by the car means he lies beneath it

parts.note: auto is an American word for a car
Psy is the South Korean singer of Gangnam Style

explanation.surface: A grim tabloid line: the examination after a Korean pop star was run over.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical examination of a body to find the cause of death is a postmortem.

clue.text: Small European airline chosen by Putin for no-frills travel?

definitions.text: chosen by Putin for no-frills travel?

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
Iberia is the Spanish national airline

explanation.surface: A budget carrier in Europe gets the Russian president's custom for cheap flights.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a joke: the Russian state has long sent its exiles and prisoners to this frozen region, a 'journey' with no frills at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The vast Russian region was the traditional destination for exile, a place the Kremlin picks for unwanted travellers.

clue.text: His Moslem ban turned out to be a policy disaster

indicators.note: turned out means overturned and emptied, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political commentator on the US travel ban judging it a fiasco.
explanation.definitionFit: The coinage, from the satire The Thick of It, describes a situation mishandled in every possible way, especially by government.

clue.text: Backing a Rhode Island cheese cake producer

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the whole string is read from the end

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island
Edam is a Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: It suggests a Rhode Island cheesecake baker, with 'backing' as financial support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheese cake' looks like one item, but the cheese is wordplay and the cake belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Portuguese island gave its name to the wine, and Madeira cake was made to be served with it, so the island is a playful source of cake.

clue.text: Manchester United leading the league? It might change!

indicators.note: leading means placed in front, so the club's initials go ahead of the next piece

parts.note: MU is the initials of Manchester United football club
a league is ranked in its table, which lists the clubs in order

explanation.surface: A football fan admits Manchester United's place at the top of the standings is not permanent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mutable is liable to alter, describing what could change.

clue.text: Vital ingredient of the Spam supply chain?

definitions.text: Vital ingredient of the Spam supply chain?

parts.words: Vital ingredient of the Spam supply chain?
parts.note: spam is junk mail sent electronically, and every message needs a destination in someone's inbox, so the target's online contact is the key component

explanation.surface: It sounds like a question about the tinned pork made by Hormel and what goes into it.
explanation.walkthrough: Spam, the canned luncheon meat, lent its name to unsolicited electronic mail; the clue's capital S hides the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Spammers cannot deliver anything without a list of inbox locations, so a contact for electronic messages is what feeds their chain.

clue.text: Mischievous Mr V. Putin — aka "The Real Power in the White House?"

definitions.text: The Real Power in the White House?

indicators.note: mischievous suggests naughty playing about, so the letters of the name are jumbled

explanation.surface: A jibe that the Russian leader is secretly the one running the US presidency.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of MR V PUTIN AKA rearrange into the name of the US president's daughter, who was a senior adviser in his first term.
explanation.definitionFit: The president's elder daughter served as a close adviser, and critics joked she held real influence there.

clue.text: Rotating air inlet

indicators.note: rotating means turning round, so the three letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: It sounds like part of a fan or engine: a spinning vent drawing in air.
explanation.definitionFit: This geographical term names a long narrow sea inlet formed by a drowned river valley.

clue.text: Complain wife's leaving door open because of this?

indicators.note: the wife leaving means her letter departs from the complaint word

parts.note: whinge is British slang for complain or moan
W is the abbreviation for wife, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A husband grumbles that his wife walked out and left the door ajar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complain' looks like a request, but it is WHINGE (British for moan), losing W.
explanation.definitionFit: A door swings open on its pivot joint, the fitting that makes opening possible.

clue.text: Strong cocktail; one's likely to get hammered!

definitions.meaning: a potent mix of Scotch whisky and Drambuie
a corroded spike of metal is driven into wood with a hammer; 'hammered' also means drunk

explanation.surface: A warning that this potent drink will leave you very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The cocktail name and an old corroded fastener share the same two words, and both get 'hammered' in a different sense.

clue.text: Cool dude raps about American slave

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the dude and the raps are read backwards together

parts.note: a cat is jazz slang for a cool guy

explanation.surface: A hip American rapper performing about slavery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the dude and the raps round together; 'raps about' tempts as a topic of song, but the slave is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thracian gladiator was a slave who led a revolt against Rome in 73 BC.

clue.text: New England states review funding for TV, radio, press

parts.note: Mass is short for Massachusetts and ME is the abbreviation for Maine, both in New England

indicators.note: review read as re-view, looking back, so the funding word is read backwards

parts.note: aid is financial support or funding

explanation.surface: Northeastern US states reconsider their financial support for broadcasting and newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Television, radio and newspapers together are the channels of communication reaching a whole population.

clue.text: Sabotage U-boat, making Trevor capsize

parts.note: a U-boat is a German submarine, a sub

indicators.note: capsize means turn upside down, and in a down clue the name is read upwards

parts.note: Trev is the usual short form of the name Trevor

explanation.surface: A war story: someone damaging a submarine and making a sailor called Trevor overturn.
explanation.definitionFit: To undermine an institution or plan from within is to sabotage it.

clue.text: Having escaped, angry enemy turned on France

parts.note: mad means angry

indicators.note: turned means flipped around, so the enemy word is read backwards

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
F is the international vehicle registration for France

explanation.surface: Someone escapes while a furious foe turns on the French.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb to make off means to flee, so its past form means having got away.

clue.text: Barred from leaving Georgia, Mr Cruz

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
Ted Cruz is a US senator from Texas

explanation.surface: A news snippet: Senator Cruz has been prevented from leaving Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: A student confined to school or college premises as punishment is said to be confined, unable to go out.

clue.text: Jesus! Tory Government must be overthrown for starters!

indicators.note: overthrown in a down clue means turned upside down, so the party word is read upwards

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party
chi, the Greek letter X, is the first letter of Christos and stands for Christ, as in the Chi-Rho symbol

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that the Conservative government must be toppled first of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' looks like 'first of all', but 'starters' is the definition: first-course dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian potato dumplings are often served as a first course, or primo, at the start of a meal.

clue.text: One pulling famous old Queen?

parts.note: the Queen Mary and Queen Elizabeth 2 are famous ocean liners, which small powerful harbour vessels tow into port

explanation.surface: It suggests someone flirting successfully with an elderly monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulling' is British slang for picking up a romantic partner, but here it means towing; the Queen is a liner.
explanation.definitionFit: A small powerful vessel that tows or pushes large ships such as liners in harbour.

clue.text: Shot of Murray in National Observer

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the newspaper name, across its two words

explanation.surface: A newspaper photo of Andy Murray printed in the National Observer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a photograph, but it is a tennis stroke; Andy Murray is a British tennis champion.
explanation.definitionFit: A high arcing stroke over an opponent's head is one of a tennis player's strokes.

clue.text: Doctor: "Forget dad running — he might claim to have bone spurs"

definitions.text: he might claim to have bone spurs

indicators.note: running means in motion, moving about, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor tells a patient to stop worrying about his jogging father.
explanation.walkthrough: Donald Trump avoided the Vietnam draft with a diagnosis of bone spurs in his heels.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dodging military conscription might claim a medical problem, as Trump did with bone spurs.

clue.text: Go off equestrian supplier when he gets undressed

indicators.note: getting undressed means losing outer clothing, so the supplier loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a saddler makes and sells saddles and harness for riders

explanation.surface: A riding-tack seller strips off and leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs that addle become rotten, as food does when it spoils.

clue.text: Wicked Tories finally stopped growth medication

indicators.note: wicked suggests something twisted or corrupt, so the party name's letters are scrambled
finally picks the final letter of stopped

explanation.surface: Evil Conservatives at last halted a drug that promotes growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic drugs used to build muscle are compounds of this chemical class, a medication for growth.

clue.text: Sigh … Klopp's sounding like an X-Men superhero!

indicators.note: sounding like signals that the spoken words are matched by the answer

parts.note: a sigh followed by the name of Jürgen Klopp, the Liverpool football manager

explanation.surface: An exasperated fan sighs that Liverpool's manager resembles a comic-book hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marvel mutant with optic blasts is a founding member of the X-Men team.

clue.text: Pompous individual, head of state, US (retd) — Fifth Amendment

indicators.note: the head of the word state is its first letter
an amendment changes things, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A retired American head of state pleads the Fifth Amendment, the right not to incriminate himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retd' is the abbreviation for retired, here taken as letters; S plus the anagram of US RETD FIFTH gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a conceited, self-important and stiffly formal person.
